scene.note: The dark boxes set a light --ink, but the colour their writing inherits was already worked out on the body.

steps.note: The body works out its colour from --ink with the value it sees there, the page's dark ink.
Lior's rule gives the box a light --ink and a dark background.
The paragraph in the box has no colour of its own, so it inherits a finished colour from the body, and the box's --ink never reaches it.
When a colour is worked out with the box's own --ink, everything in the box inherits the light one, and follows it when it changes.
The footer is dark too and sets the same light --ink.
Its address, opening times and label inherit the body's dark colour, in the same way.
With a colour worked out on the footer itself, all its writing is light.

value.label: what keeps its colour
values: the notice and its bold line

steps.note: The rest of the page keeps its dark ink, and the colours of its own.
A fix for the whole page, such as a colour on every element, also stops a colour reaching the elements meant to inherit it.
With the fix on the two dark boxes only, they are light inside and nothing else changes.
